name: DUDE: Document Understanding Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark
description: DUDE (Document Understanding Dataset and Evaluation) is a large-scale, multi-domain, multi-page visual question answering benchmark presented at ICCV 2023 and featured in the ICDAR 2023 Competition on Document UnderstanDing of Everything. Designed to stress-test real-world document understanding across long layouts and diverse visual styles, DUDE comprises 41,491 question-answer pairs spanning 4,974 visually rich documents with arbitrary page lengths (ranging from single-page sheets up to multi-hundred-page reports). Documents are sampled across 8 distinct business and administrative domains (financial, legal, scientific, government, consumer products, marketing, manuals, and technical reports), testing fine-grained visual parsing, multi-page reading order, cross-page entity resolution, and tabular reasoning.

size.notes: Multi-page PDF archives, Amazon Textract pre-computed OCR structures, and JSONL question-answer evaluation ground truth.

provenance.collection_method: Multi-domain sampling of native digital and scanned multi-page business documents, paired with expert and crowd annotations designed to test cross-page synthesis and long-context reasoning.
provenance.curation_notes: Encompasses diverse real-world documents ranging up to hundreds of pages per file. Explicitly avoids synthetic document templates.
data_sources: Public corporate financial filings, technical manuals, scientific articles, and legal documents
